test_title: SSC MTS Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14 July 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The larger diagonal of a rhombus is 150% of its smaller diagonal, and its area is 432 cm². Find the length (in cm) of the side of the rhombus?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **diagonals** d₁ : d₂ = 100 : 150 = 2 : 3.

Area = 1/2 × 2x × 3x = 3x² = 432 ⇒ x² = 144 ⇒ x = 12.

Half-diagonals are 12 and 18.

**Side of rhombus** = √(12² + 18²) = √(144 + 324) = √468 = 6√13 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6√13 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Area of Rhombus** = 432 cm²

Ratio of **diagonals** (d₁ : d₂) = 1 : 1.5 = 2 : 3

**Formula Used:**

Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

Side (s) = √[(d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f1fa6a147e06ad4b3e10b25cae0ce172a893ab0f2dd3b4ca833712e18fe776dd.png] 

Let the smaller diagonal d₁ be 2x and the larger diagonal d₂ be 3x.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 2x × 3x = 432

⇒ 3x² = 432

⇒ x² = 144

⇒ x = 12

⇒ d₁ = 2 × 12 = 24 cm

⇒ d₂ = 3 × 12 = 36 cm

⇒ Side = √[(24/2)² + (36/2)²]

⇒ Side = √[12² + 18²]

⇒ Side = √[144 + 324]

⇒ Side = √468

⇒ Side = √(36 × 13) = 6√13 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6√13 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

A rhombus is a quadrilateral with all four sides equal. Diagonals bisect each other at 90°.

Perimeter of Rhombus

Perimeter = 4 × side = 4s.

Relation between Side and Diagonals

4s² = d₁² + d₂², where s is the side and d₁, d₂ are the diagonals.</p
